alignments.note: The waw is rendered by the clause-opening connective “Then.”
The inflected verb takes its subject pronoun, auxiliary, and phrasal rendering “send abroad,” headed on “send.”
The anarthrous noun licenses the supplied definite article in “the trumpet.”
The blast noun is rendered attributively as “loud” in “loud trumpet.”
The ASV consolidates the two Hebrew date expressions as “on the tenth day of the seventh month”; the later prepositions supply “on” and “of,” leaving this initial temporal preposition unrepresented.
This first article of “the month the seventh” takes the single English “the,” fronted before “seventh.”
This is the month modified by “seventh” and retained in the ASV’s consolidated date expression.
The noun and its agreeing adjective have two Hebrew articles but the ASV writes one “the”; the noun’s earlier article takes it under the first-article rule.
The calendrical numeral is expanded as “tenth day”; “day” completes the English substantive expression, while “tenth” carries the numeral’s lexeme.
The preposition on the resumptive month expression supplies the surviving genitive relation “of.”
The ASV suppresses this article along with the resumptive second occurrence of “month”; the written “the” belongs to the retained first month expression.
Hebrew repeats “month” in “the tenth of the month,” but the ASV consolidates it with the earlier “seventh month” and renders the noun only once, on s007.
The construct noun takes only “day”; the fronted article is licensed by the article on its nomen rectum.
The nomen rectum’s article is rendered as the “the” fronted before the construct noun in “the day of atonement.”
As the nomen rectum, the noun takes both “of” and “atonement,” headed on the noun.
The inflected verb takes its subject pronoun, auxiliary, and phrasal rendering “send abroad,” headed on “send.”
The anarthrous noun licenses the supplied definite article in “the trumpet.”
The preposition’s distributive force is rendered as “throughout.”
The pronominal suffix is rendered by the possessive “your.”

review_notes: The ASV consolidates Hebrew “in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month” into “on the tenth day of the seventh month.” The retained “month” and its article are assigned to the first occurrence because “seventh” modifies that occurrence; the later month and article are resumptive and unrepresented, while its preposition supplies “of.”
